_comment: BlocklistStoreTests.swift (Swift). Three implementations of one rule; a
divergence means a domain is blocked on the Mac and reachable in Chrome,
or the reverse, with nothing to signal it.
The `block: false` half of this table is not padding — it is the more
important half. A false positive here takes out an entire site, and these
cases are the regression net that keeps county councils, analytics

cases.why: the core case: a brand-new domain no list has yet, caught on a token
substring matching is what catches a concatenated label with no separators
a subdomain of an adult host still matches
CRITICAL: an innocent token must not grant the rest of the host immunity
a trailing digit run is hostname decoration, stripped before matching
a LEADING digit is a Franco-Arabic letter and must survive
Essex County Council — the canonical Scunthorpe-problem failure
'anal' inside 'analytics' — would break measurement on every site
'ass' inside 'assets' — would break the asset host of half the web
CRITICAL: 'sks' inside 'tasks' — as a substring this single Franco-Arabic term would block a large fraction of the web
an absolute FQDN's trailing dot must not bypass the keyword layer, exactly as it must not bypass the domain list
